headline: Highest risk is prompt-injection via shared conversational content; other risks are mostly low-to-medium because Rasa is allowlisted-network and the second profile has no write surfaces.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Rasa ingests conversational text and can call external channels, so attacker-controlled content can reach its dialogue logic. system_prompts_leaks is a prompt-leakage corpus, which increases the chance that malicious instructions are present in content passed through the pair. No shared channel is explicit, so this is inferred rather than directly evidenced.
conditions: IF content from system_prompts_leaks is forwarded into Rasa conversations or training data
IF a human operator copy-pastes B-derived text into A without sanitization
mitigations: Add a strict content separator and instruction filter before any B-derived text reaches A.
Review one sample conversation path for hidden instructions.
Disable any auto-forwarding from B outputs into A.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all bridged messages.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Rasa touches text and voice and has allowlisted egress, but no secrets or shared workspace are shown. system_prompts_leaks has no data classes touched and no egress, so the pair does not obviously create a leakage path beyond manual handling. Uncertainty remains because the bridge is undocumented.
conditions: IF operators place sensitive transcripts into Rasa and then export them into B-related workflows
IF a shared workspace is introduced outside the profiles
mitigations: Keep sensitive transcripts out of any shared folder.
Confirm Rasa egress allowlist excludes third-party logging.
Review one export path for accidental transcript copying.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Rasa does not support multiple instances, and system_prompts_leaks exposes no write, network, or OAuth scopes. With no overlapping mutable resource in the profiles, a write-write conflict pathway is not supported by the evidence.
conditions: IF a shared writable directory is added outside the profiles
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate directories.
Avoid concurrent writes to any shared artifact.
requires-engineering: add file locking if a shared store is introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Rasa can generate conversational outputs that downstream systems may treat as authoritative, but system_prompts_leaks is not shown to take actions or verify facts. The pair therefore has a limited cascade risk mainly if operators reuse B-derived text as trusted input to A or vice versa.
conditions: IF B-derived text is used as authoritative content in A responses
IF an operator routes A outputs into another automation step
mitigations: Require human review before reusing generated text.
Mark B-derived content as untrusted in prompts.
requires-engineering: add verification gates before automation.

E_compliance.rationale: Rasa touches text and voice, which can include regulated content, while system_prompts_leaks is a source-available corpus with no stated residency or retention controls. The profiles do not show a direct residency or certification mismatch, so compliance risk is limited to undocumented handling choices.
conditions: IF regulated transcripts are stored in B-linked repositories
IF retention policies differ for the same transcript class
mitigations: Check whether any regulated data enters B-linked storage.
Remove regulated samples from shared notes.
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion policies.
